audit.description: Canonical findings index for the comprehensive repository audit scaffold.

id.description: Stable finding identifier unique within this audit index.

title.description: Concise finding title describing the observed risk or defect.

evidence_tier.description: Report section bucket selected from schema.allowed_values.evidence_tier.

owner_domain.description: Primary ownership area such as backend, frontend, docs, tests, security, operations, or infrastructure.

source_report.description: Relative path to the report file or review artifact where the finding was first recorded.

fields.summary: Observed behavior, code fact, log excerpt summary, or verification result.
fields.locations: Array of relative repository paths, optionally with line references.

affected_paths.description: Relative repository paths affected by the finding.

findings.title: Admin impersonation response advertises a 15 minute TTL but mints a normal access token

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-authnz-admin-001.
The impersonation endpoint returns a 15 minute expires_in_minutes value but calls create_access_token without a TTL override, so jwt_service uses the global access-token lifetime.
Existing tests assert response metadata and claims but do not decode the issued JWT and verify exp minus iat.

findings.recommendation: Add an explicit impersonation token creation path that accepts the 15 minute TTL, marks the token as an impersonation token, returns the actual expiry, and add a regression test that decodes the token and verifies exp minus iat matches the impersonation TTL.

findings.title: Impersonation actor metadata is not preserved for durable audit attribution

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-authnz-admin-002.
The endpoint adds impersonated_by and impersonation JWT claims, but downstream token decoding and AuthContext creation preserve only subject/org/team scope claims.
Comparable high-risk user administration operations use privileged-action verification and durable audit events, while impersonation issuance records only a process log line.

findings.recommendation: Treat impersonation token issuance as a privileged admin action: require step-up reauthentication or an admin reauth token, emit a durable mandatory audit event on issuance, and propagate impersonation metadata into AuthContext or request state so downstream audit events include both actor and subject.

findings.title: Admin impersonation uses SQLite placeholders through a raw PostgreSQL connection path

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-authnz-admin-003.

The impersonation endpoint acquires a raw pool connection and executes SQL with question-mark placeholders; the PostgreSQL acquire path yields raw asyncpg connections and placeholder conversion is limited to DatabasePool helper methods.
The existing unit test mocks a generic async connection and does not exercise PostgreSQL placeholder conversion.

findings.recommendation: Replace raw connection calls with repository methods or DatabasePool.fetchone so placeholder normalization is centralized. Add a backend-agnostic unit test or PostgreSQL fixture test for the impersonation user and role lookups.

findings.title: SQLite Media DB upgrades before v22 cannot reach current schema from packaged migrations

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-db-migrations-data-durability-001.
A file-backed DB with schema_version 8 failed migrate_to_version(23) because packaged migrations are missing versions 9 through 22 for the Media DB chain.
Existing coverage validates the v22-to-v23 backfill only and does not cover representative older Media DB versions.

findings.recommendation: Split package migrations by database or domain, or otherwise scope DatabaseMigrator so Media DB upgrades do not consume Prompt Studio versions. Provide a contiguous supported Media DB migration chain, or explicitly reject unsupported legacy versions with a documented backup/export/rebuild workflow, and add package-directory upgrade tests for representative legacy versions older than v22.

findings.title: Generic SQLite migrations can leave partial DDL after a failed multi-statement script

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-db-migrations-data-durability-002.
Runtime reproduction applied a two-statement migration where the first statement created a table and the second failed; the migration was recorded as failed, but the created table remained present.
The executor applies SQL, inserts the migration ledger row, and updates schema_version in separate commit windows.

findings.recommendation: Execute each migration, success ledger insert or delete, and schema_version update inside one explicit transaction boundary, preferably BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Normalize migration files so the migrator owns transaction control, or reject and handle files with embedded transaction control explicitly, and add regression coverage for a failing multi-statement script that leaves no partial DDL behind.

findings.title: Billing settings call public billing routes that the OSS API intentionally omits

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-webui-extension-api-contracts-001.
The settings UI shows and loads billing data based only on multi-user login state, then calls billing plan, subscription, usage, invoice, checkout, portal, cancel, and resume routes.
The backend test asserts the OSS app registers no public billing routes, and the OpenAPI verifier carries those billing paths as reviewed exceptions outside the OSS contract.

findings.recommendation: Hide or disable the billing tab and billing loaders/actions unless a hosted billing capability is advertised by the backend or isHostedTldwDeployment is true. Keep hosted-only billing paths out of the OSS ClientPath contract, or isolate them behind a hosted-only client adapter so the OpenAPI verifier can fail unexpected public-route drift.

findings.title: Speech playground TTS streaming uses query-token WebSocket auth rejected by default

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-webui-extension-api-contracts-002.
The Speech playground opens /api/v1/audio/stream/tts with a token query parameter and sends the first frame as a prompt payload instead of an auth frame.
The backend disables query-token WebSocket auth by default, accepts it only behind AUDIO_WS_ALLOW_QUERY_TOKEN_AUTH, and has a focused unit test reproducing rejection for audio.stream.tts.

findings.recommendation: Change the browser client to use the backend-supported initial auth frame before sending the TTS request payload, or add a shared WebSocket auth helper matching the working voice-assistant protocol. Do not depend on query-string tokens for default WebSocket streaming flows.

findings.title: Published worker images are not built by the PR container gate
findings.owner_domain: CI, Deployment, Operations, and Release Surfaces

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-ci-deployment-operations-release-001.
publish-docker.yml publishes worker and audio-worker Dockerfiles, while container-build-check.yml only builds prod, webui, and admin-ui images.

findings.recommendation: Add worker and audio-worker entries to container-build-check.yml, or remove them from publish-docker.yml if they are no longer supported published artifacts. Prefer adding a minimal runtime smoke or image inspection step that verifies the expected command, non-root user, and core imports for every published image.

findings.title: Published worker images run as root and keep build tooling in runtime layers
findings.owner_domain: CI, Deployment, Operations, and Release Surfaces

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-ci-deployment-operations-release-002.
Worker and audio GPU worker Dockerfiles keep compiler, network, and build tooling in final layers and have no USER directive, while Dockerfile.prod creates and switches to appuser.

findings.recommendation: Align worker images with Dockerfile.prod: use multi-stage builds, remove build-only packages from final stages, create a fixed non-root runtime user, chown only required writable paths, and add image checks to CI. For GPU workers, document any required device permissions separately from Linux user identity.

findings.title: actionlint gate covers only a small subset of workflow files
findings.owner_domain: CI, Deployment, Operations, and Release Surfaces

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-ci-deployment-operations-release-003.

The actionlint workflow triggers on workflow and action changes, but its lint command enumerates only 8 workflow files while the repository has 38 workflow files, excluding multiple required and release-sensitive workflows.

findings.recommendation: Run actionlint against all workflows and composite actions, or generate the target list from the filesystem in CI. If a workflow must be excluded, record the explicit exclusion and reason in the workflow.

findings.title: SBOM workflow skips Bun-based frontend dependencies
findings.owner_domain: CI, Deployment, Operations, and Release Surfaces

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-ci-deployment-operations-release-004.

The repository uses apps/bun.lock and admin-ui/bun.lock with no package-lock.json found; sbom.yml only checks package-lock paths and can publish a Python-only SBOM while Node validation is skipped or continue-on-error.

findings.recommendation: Add Bun-aware SBOM generation for apps/bun.lock and admin-ui/bun.lock, include all frontend workspaces, and fail the SBOM job when an expected ecosystem cannot be represented. Make validation required once the generator coverage is complete.

findings.title: Dependency update automation omits nested JS, Python, and Go package roots
findings.owner_domain: CI, Deployment, Operations, and Release Surfaces

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-ci-deployment-operations-release-005.
dependabot.yml configures root pip and GitHub Actions updates only, while the dependency-manifest inventory lists maintained nested frontend, admin, MCP package, SDK, tool, and Go module roots.

findings.recommendation: Add update automation for every maintained package root. If Dependabot cannot handle the Bun lockfiles reliably, use Renovate or another Bun-aware updater for apps and admin-ui, add gomod coverage for tools/tldw-agent, and add nested Python package coverage or an explicit documented exclusion for packages not intended to be maintained independently.

findings.title: Kubernetes sample Secret ships an invalid DATABASE_URL and default password
findings.owner_domain: CI, Deployment, Operations, and Release Surfaces

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-ci-deployment-operations-release-006.

The sample Secret embeds a literal ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD} in DATABASE_URL and a concrete default POSTGRES_PASSWORD; Kubernetes stringData does not interpolate the variable, so the app and Postgres receive mismatched credentials.

findings.recommendation: Replace the sample with non-runnable placeholders plus explicit generation instructions, or derive DATABASE_URL from separate env vars at runtime. If keeping a complete sample, duplicate a clearly generated example value consistently and add comments requiring rotation before deployment.

findings.title: Processing-only media endpoints bypass the media.create permission gate

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-media-ingestion-storage-001.

Several processing endpoints authenticate through get_request_user but omit the MEDIA_CREATE permission and media.create RBAC rate-limit dependencies used by persistent and comparable ingestion routes.
Comparable add/video/web scraping/ingest job routes require MEDIA_CREATE, but no equivalent no-permission denial tests were found for the processing-only endpoints.

findings.recommendation: Introduce a shared dependency bundle for all media ingestion and processing routes, or define a separate explicit media.process permission if these endpoints intentionally require a different entitlement. Add regression tests that override the principal with no media permissions and assert 403 for each processing endpoint that accepts user media or remote input.

findings.title: MediaWiki ingest persists into shared single-user content and vector namespaces

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-media-ingestion-storage-002.
The MediaWiki ingest endpoint calls the core importer with database and vector storage enabled without taking current_user, get_media_db_for_user, or a request-scoped writer.

The core importer falls back to managed_media_database with client_id mediawiki_import and constructs vector storage with SINGLE_USER_FIXED_ID, producing shared single-user content and vector namespaces.

findings.recommendation: Refactor the MediaWiki endpoint to require current_user and get_media_db_for_user, then thread a request-scoped media writer and vector user ID into import_mediawiki_dump and _store_mediawiki_chunks_in_vector_db. Add multi-user tests proving user A's MediaWiki ingest is not visible in user B's media DB or vector namespace.

findings.title: Original file storage can orphan permanent files when MediaFiles row insertion fails

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-media-ingestion-storage-003.

When keep_original_file is true, persistence stores the original file before inserting the MediaFiles row; DB errors are treated as noncritical and do not trigger compensating deletion even though the filesystem backend exposes delete.
The current regression test covers the happy path and does not simulate insert_media_file raising after storage succeeds.

findings.recommendation: Make the storage-plus-registration sequence compensating. If insert_media_file fails after storage.store returns, call await storage.delete(storage_path) and include cleanup failures in the warning or log path. Add a unit test with a fake storage backend and a DB double whose insert_media_file raises, asserting the stored path is deleted.

findings.title: Header-declared oversized audio downloads are not covered because the regression test is a no-op

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-media-ingestion-storage-004.

download_audio_file has a Content-Length fail-fast size check and streaming guard, but the header-over-limit test builds a fake oversized response without calling the function or asserting an exception.

findings.recommendation: Complete the test by invoking download_audio_file with the fake response downloader, asserting AudioFileSizeError, and asserting the expected target path was not created.

findings.title: Alternate LLM/RAG generation routes drift from virtual-key endpoint and max-call enforcement

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-chat-rag-llm-001.

The primary RAG search route declares RBAC rate limit, MEDIA_READ, TokenScopeGuard with endpoint_id rag.search, and daily RAG limit, but adjacent RAG batch/simple/stream/advanced routes omit some endpoint-scope and count enforcement.
Character completion, chat document generation, and embeddings routes have route-level or middleware differences from the TokenScopeGuard path that enforces allowed endpoints and max-call counters.

findings.recommendation: Give every externally reachable route that spends LLM/RAG/embedding resources a stable endpoint ID and a shared enforcement dependency. Add TokenScopeGuard or equivalent central guards to RAG alternate routes, character completion routes, document generation routes, and embeddings routes, and add HTTP tests with virtual API keys limited by allowed_endpoints, allowed_paths, allowed_methods, and max_calls for each alternate path.

findings.title: RAG search endpoints log raw user queries at info level

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-chat-rag-llm-002.
unified_search_endpoint and advanced_search_endpoint log full query text at info level, while simple_search_endpoint demonstrates a safer query_hash and query length pattern in the same module.

findings.recommendation: Replace raw query logging with the safer pattern already used by /rag/simple: log a non-security hash, query length, user/request metadata, and feature flags instead of full query text. Keep full query payloads out of info-level logs; if operational debugging needs them, require an explicit debug-only opt-in with redaction.

findings.title: Async workflow runs are handed to an in-process daemon-thread scheduler with no durable recovery for queued runs

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-jobs-scheduler-workflows-001.

HTTP ad-hoc workflow runs and the durable Scheduler workflow_run handler create workflow run rows and then hand execution to WorkflowEngine.submit, which delegates async execution to an in-memory WorkflowScheduler queue and daemon threads.
The orphan reaper covers stale running step rows and the maintenance service is checkpoint/VACUUM oriented, not queued workflow row recovery.

findings.recommendation: Execute workflow runs end-to-end inside a durable Jobs or Scheduler worker, or add a startup/periodic repair loop that finds queued/running workflow rows without active execution and requeues them idempotently. Avoid daemon threads for durable work, or make them a thin local executor backed by durable queue state and explicit shutdown/drain semantics.

findings.title: Recurring workflow and ACP schedule fires submit non-idempotent Scheduler tasks

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-jobs-scheduler-workflows-002.
Recurring workflow and ACP schedule fires call core_scheduler.submit without idempotency_key, and the downstream workflow_run handler creates a new UUID run with idempotency_key=None.

The core Scheduler and SQLite backend already support unique non-null idempotency keys, but inspected workflow scheduler tests do not cover multi-process schedule ownership or duplicate schedule-fire dedupe.

findings.recommendation: Add a deterministic idempotency key for each schedule fire, namespaced by handler, schedule ID, owner/user, and fire time window. Pass that key to core_scheduler.submit and propagate it into workflow run creation where appropriate. Alternatively or additionally, add a distributed leader/lease for the recurring APScheduler service. Add tests that submit the same logical schedule fire twice and assert one Scheduler task or workflow run.

findings.title: Workflow research adapters bypass centralized outbound HTTP controls

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-integrations-providers-001.

Workflow research search and bibliography adapters use raw httpx.AsyncClient for arXiv PDF URLs, PubMed, Semantic Scholar, Google Patents, and DOI resolution, without the central HTTP client or outbound URL policy helpers.
Existing tests cover test-mode behavior and sanitized backend errors but did not show egress denial, proxy avoidance, or centralized client use for these workflow research calls.

findings.recommendation: Route workflow research outbound calls through tldw_Server_API.app.core.http_client.afetch or create_async_client. Enforce the same outbound URL policy used by web search and scraping before fetching user-supplied or context-derived URLs. Add regression tests for blocked private/loopback URLs, trust_env=False behavior, and the direct pdf_url download path.

findings.title: Tokenizer resolver bypasses centralized outbound HTTP controls

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-integrations-providers-002.

tokenizer_resolver builds provider-native tokenizer/counting endpoints and sends them through a private _http_post implementation that imports requests and calls requests.post directly, bypassing the central HTTP helpers used by primary LLM adapters.
Tokenizer tests cover adapter selection, payloads, provider metadata, and some host guard behavior, but not central client use, egress denial, or proxy avoidance.

findings.recommendation: Replace _http_post with the central HTTP client helpers, or wrap it with equivalent egress/proxy defaults and test coverage. Add regression tests for private/loopback/tokenizer URLs denied by policy, environment proxy avoidance, and commercial provider base URL overrides. If local tokenizer endpoints are intentionally supported, gate them behind an explicit local-provider allow option rather than bypassing the central path.

findings.title: Weather provider uses raw httpx for API-key-bearing request

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-integrations-providers-003.

The weather provider imports httpx, sets http_client_factory to httpx.Client, builds OpenWeather params containing appid, and sends the request with the raw factory rather than the central HTTP client.
The URL is fixed to OpenWeather, so SSRF surface is narrower; the remaining concern is inconsistent policy and environment proxy exposure for an API-key-bearing request.

findings.recommendation: Use tldw_Server_API.app.core.http_client.fetch or create_client for OpenWeather requests, keeping the existing test injection seam if useful. Add a small regression test that verifies the weather request client inherits central proxy/egress defaults or explicitly sets trust_env=False.

findings.title: Scoped AuthNZ JWT restrictions are bypassed on ACP and sandbox WebSocket endpoints

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-mcp-sandbox-agent-protocol-001.

HTTP scoped-token enforcement validates scope, allowed endpoint/path/method, quota, and schedule claims, but ACP WebSocket auth verifies JWTs directly and only applies required_scope on the API-key path.

Sandbox WebSocket auth verifies access tokens directly and returns subject IDs while the socket can accept stdin frames for interactive runs; existing focused tests cover read-only API-key rejection but not scoped AuthNZ JWT claims.

findings.recommendation: Authenticate ACP and sandbox WebSocket bearer tokens through the same scoped-token enforcement used by HTTP endpoints, including scope, allowed_endpoints, allowed_methods, allowed_paths, quota, and schedule claims. Add scoped-JWT tests for rejected ACP stream, ACP SSH, and sandbox run stream handshakes.

findings.title: ACP reconnect WebSocket replay leaks WSBroadcaster subscriptions/tasks

evidence.summary: Original candidate ID: CANDIDATE-mcp-sandbox-agent-protocol-002.

The ACP reconnect branch creates and starts a local WSBroadcaster when last_sequence is present, but endpoint cleanup unregisters only the runner callback, stream, and quota release without removing the connection or stopping the broadcaster.

WSBroadcaster.start subscribes to the bus and spawns a consume task, stop cancels and unsubscribes, and the event bus stores subscribers by a fixed consumer id that repeated reconnects replace while stale tasks remain blocked on old queues.

findings.recommendation: Retain the reconnect WSBroadcaster and connection id in acp_session_stream, remove the connection and call stop in finally, and use a per-connection consumer id or a single shared session broadcaster. Add an endpoint-level reconnect-disconnect test that verifies the bus subscriber and broadcaster task are cleaned up.

findings.title: Workflow continuation resumes are fire-and-forget tasks outside durable scheduler ownership

evidence.summary: Workflow run retry, approval, rejection, orphan requeue, and research checkpoint resume paths spawn engine.continue_run through local asyncio.create_task calls rather than durable Jobs or Scheduler ownership.

Existing tests cover successful continuation and pre-schedule bridge exceptions, but the specialist did not find coverage for accepted create_task continuations that later fail, are cancelled on shutdown, or are lost before execution.

The specialist report records this as distinct from AUDIT-2026-06-27-JOBS-001 because these continuation paths bypass even the in-process WorkflowScheduler.submit handoff; both findings should be reconciled under one workflow execution ownership model.

findings.recommendation: Persist continuation intent and submit approvals, rejections, retries, orphan requeues, and research checkpoint resumes through Jobs or Scheduler with deterministic idempotency keys based on run ID, step ID, continuation cause, and target step. Reconcile the execution ownership model with AUDIT-2026-06-27-JOBS-001 and add tests for post-schedule failure, shutdown before execution, duplicate resume, and research wait retryability.

findings.title: Audio WebSocket query-token drift extends beyond Speech playground TTS to STT and voice chat

evidence.summary: The extension STT bridge opens /api/v1/audio/stream/transcribe with a query token and sends audio frames without an initial auth frame.
The voice-chat path builds /api/v1/audio/chat/stream with a query token, opens it directly, and sends config as the first structured message instead of auth.

The backend documents legacy query-token auth as disabled by default for transcribe, voice chat, and TTS WebSocket routes; the shared auth helper defaults _allow_query_token_auth() to false and then waits for an initial auth message.

Existing backend tests prove default query-token-disabled behavior for the shared TTS helper, while several audio WebSocket tests explicitly enable the legacy fallback and therefore do not cover the browser clients' default production contract.

findings.recommendation: Replace browser audio WebSocket URL builders with a shared helper that opens the bare route and sends the backend-supported initial auth frame before config, prompt, or audio frames. Add client and backend contract coverage for default query-token-disabled behavior on STT, voice chat, and TTS.

findings.title: Python runtime and release installs lack a committed lockfile or constraints

evidence.summary: The tracked lock-like files cover Bun, mock OpenAI requirements, and the Go agent, but no root Python uv.lock, constraints file, Poetry lock, Pipfile lock, or backend requirements file was found.
The backend dependency graph lives in pyproject.toml with many open lower-bound ranges and unbounded package names.
Production, worker, audio worker, required CI, security, publish, RC, and setup-python-deps installs resolve Python dependencies without a committed lock or constraints input.

findings.recommendation: Add a committed lock or constraints workflow for supported Python install profiles, then make production Docker builds, required backend/security gates, and publish/RC jobs install with locked or constrained resolution. Keep separate runtime and dev/test profiles if needed, and document any intentionally floating optional extras.

findings.title: Static-analysis and CI gates bootstrap mutable external tooling

evidence.summary: The actionlint workflow executes a branch-head remote installer from raw.githubusercontent.com, so a workflow-lint gate runs mutable upstream shell code.
Security, pre-commit, and SBOM workflows install Bandit, PyYAML, pre-commit, pytest, CycloneDX, and Node SBOM tooling without pinned tool versions.

Required setup workflows and the setup-python-deps action use moving action tags or unconstrained package installs, while publish workflows already demonstrate local SHA-pinning patterns for higher-risk release jobs.

findings.recommendation: Replace branch-head remote installers with pinned releases and checksums or pinned action SHAs, pin static-analysis tool versions through the same constraints process as application dependencies, and pin third-party actions in required/static-analysis workflows with scheduled update automation.

findings.title: Bandit app baseline mixes production code with in-package tests

evidence.summary: The existing Bandit summary scanned tldw_Server_API/app and reported 4,818 results: 4,792 low, 26 medium, and 0 high.
Most medium Bandit records are test-only paths under tldw_Server_API/app/core/MCP_unified/tests, which lives inside the app tree and is also listed in pyproject.toml pytest testpaths.

.bandit excludes virtualenvs and node_modules, but does not exclude in-package tests; production-looking B608 records and the admin E2E temp-dir record were source-reviewed and not promoted to new security findings.

findings.recommendation: Split Bandit execution into a production profile that excludes in-package tests and a separate test-profile scan. Keep the reviewed B608 dynamic-SQL patterns under explicit allowlist or refactor them to helper builders so future Bandit deltas are easier to triage.
